claims.statement: deepagents-code (dcode) is a prebuilt terminal coding agent that packages the deepagents SDK harness together with a terminal experience, persistence, tools, skills, and optional sandboxed execution, as a reference implementation.

dcode has two runtime halves that run in separate processes: a terminal client that owns presentation and input (interactive or headless output plus approvals), and an agent server that owns the agent runtime and connects the model, tools, memory, skills, and backend.
`python -m deepagents_code` invokes the package's lazy `cli_main` entry point, which defers importing `main.py` and its CLI startup machinery until the command is actually used.

Normal interactive and headless runs use `start_server_and_get_agent` to resolve and export `ServerConfig`, scaffold a temporary LangGraph project with a SQLite checkpointer module, start `langgraph dev`, wait for graph readiness, and return a workspace-bound `RemoteAgent`; failed or cancelled startup stops the owned server.

The Textual runner accepts raw resume intent and server construction parameters, starts server work in the background when it owns the server, and documents asynchronous resume resolution; focused app tests cover deferred startup, resume ordering, queue/restart recovery, approval interaction, and teardown.

The server validates every execution request against a durable per-thread workspace binding, rebuilds a workspace runtime when its full runtime identity changes, but rejects access-policy drift; runtime caching is LRU-bounded and a configured sandbox is reserved to one workspace per server process.

Workspace diagnostics persist and compare only a bounded allowlist of policy fields; paths, model specifications and parameters, prompts, environment values, and credentials are excluded from diagnostic snapshots and reporting.

For a workspace outside the launch project, `ServerConfig.resolve_workspace` drops launch-project MCP configuration, sandbox setup, and extension paths, and resolves extension trust for the target project instead of reusing the original project's policy.

Server graph construction creates built-in tools, conditionally adds web search, and loads MCP tools with project context and trust; discovery uses throwaway sessions while a process-wide MCP session manager opens real sessions lazily for tool invocation, and only explicitly read-only MCP tools are exposed to criteria/grading context.

`RemoteAgent` wraps LangGraph `RemoteGraph` for HTTP and SSE execution, adds the cached per-thread workspace descriptor to each stream context, converts serialized message and interrupt payloads for the client, and keeps graph state retrieval separate from session-cost reconciliation.

The ACP CLI mode is in-process and creates a graph per ACP session from that session's model and cwd rather than using the normal remote-server workspace cache; its Auto adapter writes trusted approval state and prompt metadata to a store before graph streaming.

Focused server and client tests lock the boundary behavior: server tests cover cached construction, startup failure signaling, workspace-specific tools and fail-closed criteria-tool selection, while remote-client tests cover streamed payload conversion, trace forwarding, and independent state and cost behavior.

`create_cli_agent` is the common graph-construction seam for server and ACP callers: it returns a compiled graph and `CompositeBackend`, composes model, persistence, tools, memory, skills, backend, approval, hooks, compaction, subagents, and extensions, and propagates an explicit filesystem-tool allowlist to synchronous subagents so delegation cannot bypass it.

Graph construction enforces the model allow policy for executable main, Auto-classifier, rubric, and subagent model strings, resolves recognized provider models with SDK retries disabled so dcode owns retries, and defers a subagent with missing credentials instead of aborting startup.

The MCP tool timeout is a manifest-backed setting with managed configuration, environment, user TOML, and a 120-second default in precedence order; only finite values from 1 through 900 seconds are accepted and invalid higher-precedence values fall through.

When MCP tools are installed, graph construction adds deadline middleware inside the server-hooks wrapper; it normalizes optional empty-string arguments, returns a named error tool message on timeout warning that the remote operation may continue and retries may duplicate work, preserves tool exceptions and cancellation, and translates recognized re-authentication failures.

Hook invocations are strict, discriminated domain events with typed context and decisions; projection validates each event-specific wire payload, JSON-projects post-tool results, maps approval and optional effort or agent identity, requires an agent transcript for SubagentStop, and rejects unsupported events or notification types.

The Textual client treats server checkpoint and stream totals as authoritative thread cost, may display request-keyed provisional stream cost until a server total settles it, discards totals for inactive threads, and warns once on an authoritative threshold crossing.

Session cost reconciliation combines graph-checkpoint cost with best-effort separately persisted side-question cost; when graph state is not settled, the result marks itself cached so the UI preserves provisional main-task spend.

The Textual adapter forwards only dictionary custom-stream payloads with `type == "subagent"` from the main-agent namespace to the app’s `SubagentPanel`, preventing nested, unrelated, and malformed events from reaching the fan-out display.

`SubagentPanel` is a UI-only live view of QuickJS `js_eval` fan-out: it groups subagent lifecycle records by eval id, tracks local phase/row state and timing, supports user phase selection and collapse, and clears or cancels local rows on new or interrupted turns without owning graph execution or persistence.

The subagent panel treats LLM/JavaScript-authored labels and errors as untrusted: it sanitizes control, escape, and bidi characters, bounds and flattens labels, and renders plain/styled Textual content rather than markup; widget tests cover escape stripping and lifecycle rendering behavior.

A positive session-cost threshold triggers a once-per-thread Textual modal only after an authoritative total is strictly above the threshold; the modal uses plain-text widgets, remains open after clicks, and Enter or Escape acknowledges it without altering session state or cancelling active work.

System-prompt smoke coverage builds a real CLI agent with a fake model and snapshots the first composed `SystemMessage` for interactive and headless modes after fixing and redacting machine-specific inputs; parameterized assertions also preserve memory and safety guidance while excluding unreachable interactive-question guidance in headless mode.

dcode configuration normally resolves through one process-wide generation so readers share a coherent snapshot; file edits take effect through an in-app default-config write or `/reload`, while a failed user TOML parse retains the last usable generation and environment resolution remains live.

An explicit `system_prompt` passed to `create_cli_agent` replaces, rather than augments, the generated prompt and its dynamic execution context; without an override, prompt generation includes model, working-directory, execution-mode, skills, and interactive-versus-headless guidance.
